framework.name: Next Generation Science Standards
framework.source: https://www.nextgenscience.org (HS performance expectations; objective wording is the school's own)

objectives.description: Plan a safe investigation, control variables, and record data with units and uncertainty.

strands.strand: HS-LS1 From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes
strands.subStrand: HS-LS1 From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes

objectives.description: Develop a model of how the parts of a multicellular organism, from cells to organ systems, work together.
Describe the four classes of biological molecules and match each to its building blocks and role.
Explain how enzymes speed up reactions and how temperature and pH change their activity.

strands.strand: HS-LS1 From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes
strands.subStrand: HS-LS1 From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes

objectives.description: Explain how the structure of DNA determines the structure of the proteins that carry out a cell's functions.
Compare prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells and name the job of each organelle.
Explain how the membrane controls what enters and leaves a cell through diffusion, osmosis and active transport.

strands.strand: HS-LS1 From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes
strands.subStrand: HS-LS1 From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes

objectives.description: Use evidence to show how carbon, hydrogen and oxygen from sugars build amino acids and other large molecules.
Model how photosynthesis transforms light energy into stored chemical energy.
Model cellular respiration as a process that breaks bonds in food molecules and releases energy for the cell.
Compare photosynthesis and cellular respiration as a cycle of matter and a flow of energy.
Model the role of mitosis in growth and in the replacement of cells in an organism.
Describe the stages of the cell cycle and explain how checkpoints help control it.
Plan an investigation of how feedback mechanisms keep an organism's internal conditions stable.
Describe how a tissue is made of specialized cells and how tissues form organs.
Explain how the body keeps blood sugar and body temperature within a narrow range.
Use a microscope to view cells, draw what is seen to scale, and calculate magnification.
Construct a scientific explanation from evidence, using a claim, evidence and reasoning.
Use measurement, significant figures and unit conversion in a laboratory report.
Classify matter as pure substances or mixtures, and separate a mixture using its properties.
Describe physical and chemical changes and give evidence that a chemical reaction has occurred.
Use the structure of the atom, including protons, neutrons and electrons, to describe isotopes and ions.
Use the periodic table to predict the patterns of electrons and the properties of elements.
Explain periodic trends in atomic radius, ionization energy and electronegativity.
Explain why a chemical reaction goes the way it does from the outermost electrons of the atoms.
Distinguish ionic, covalent and metallic bonds and write formulas and names for common compounds.
Plan an investigation of how forces between particles explain the properties of substances.
Draw Lewis structures and predict the shape and polarity of simple molecules.
Use the conservation of mass to count atoms and quantities in a balanced reaction.
Balance chemical equations and classify reactions as synthesis, decomposition, replacement or combustion.
Convert between moles, mass and number of particles using molar mass and Avogadro's number.
Calculate the mass of product from the mass of reactant, and find the limiting reactant.
Calculate percent yield and explain why an actual yield is less than the theoretical yield.
Predict whether a double replacement reaction forms a precipitate using solubility rules.
Investigate how thermal energy moves between two systems until they reach the same temperature.
Analyze lab data, identify sources of error, and report a conclusion supported by the data.
Design an investigation, collect data with uncertainty, and present it in a graph with a line of best fit.

strands.strand: HS-PS2 Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions
strands.subStrand: HS-PS2 Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions

objectives.description: Distinguish distance from displacement and speed from velocity, and calculate each.
Describe motion in one dimension using position, velocity and acceleration graphs.
Apply the equations of motion for constant acceleration to solve problems.
Analyze free fall and explain why objects with different masses fall together when air resistance is small.
Add and resolve vectors graphically and by components.
Analyze projectile motion by treating the horizontal and vertical motions separately.
Analyze data to support the claim that the net force on an object equals its mass times its acceleration.
Draw free-body diagrams and find the net force on an object.
State and apply Newton's first and third laws to everyday situations.
Calculate the force of friction and of tension, and solve problems on inclined planes.
Use laws of gravitation to describe forces between objects at a distance and explain weight.
Describe uniform circular motion and identify the centripetal force in a given situation.
Use the conservation of momentum to predict the outcome of an interaction between two objects.
Design a device that reduces the force on an object during a collision, and test it.
Relate impulse to change in momentum and apply it to a car crash or a ball hit by a bat.
Use a model to calculate how kinetic and potential energy trade off in a moving system.
Communicate the results of an investigation of motion in a short lab report.
Use anatomical terms for position, planes and body cavities to describe where structures lie.
List the levels of organization of the human body from chemicals to the whole organism.

strands.strand: HS-LS1 From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes
strands.subStrand: HS-LS1 From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes

objectives.description: Explain how negative feedback keeps body temperature, blood glucose and fluid balance stable.
Describe the biological molecules of the body and the structure and function of the cell and its organelles.
Identify the four tissue types and match each to its structure and function.

strands.strand: HS-LS1 From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes
strands.subStrand: HS-LS1 From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes

objectives.description: Describe how tissues combine to form organs and how organ systems interact.
Describe the layers of the skin and its roles in protection, temperature control and sensation.
Explain how the skin heals after a cut or a burn and how burns are classified.
Name the major bones and classify them by shape, and explain how bones grow, repair and support the body.
Compare the structure and range of motion of fibrous, cartilaginous and synovial joints.
Compare skeletal, cardiac and smooth muscle by structure, control and location.
Explain how skeletal muscle contracts, using the sliding filament model.
Name the major muscles of the body and describe the actions of prime movers, antagonists and synergists.

strands.strand: HS-LS1 From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes
strands.subStrand: HS-LS1 From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes

objectives.description: Link cellular respiration in muscle cells to the energy demands of exercise.
Describe the structure of a neuron and how an action potential travels along it.
Explain how a signal crosses a synapse and how a reflex arc works.
Describe the main regions of the brain and the roles of the central and peripheral nervous systems.
Dissect or model an organ system and report what the structures show about their function.
